sources.own_factual_extraction: The study places the Sarysu across the Kazakh uplands and western Betpakdala margin. It forms from Zhaman-Sarysu and Zhaksy-Sarysu, flows generally west, southwest and then south, and receives Kara-Kengir before a largely tributary-free lower reach. Its usual named-river length is 761 km; a hydrological main path measured from Kairakty through Zhaman-Sarysu exceeds 950 km. Floodwater reaches Lake Telekol only in some years and otherwise dissipates in alluvial deposits. The upper and lower segments therefore need distinct naming and seasonal interpretations. Russian and Kazakh titles use Сарысу; the English title uses Sarysu. The cited Figure 1 page is blank in the acquired PDF.
scope_limits: Research usage and geographic synthesis, not a formal name-register decision.
No inspectable map exists on printed page 158 of this acquired PDF; the missing figure is not reconstructed or treated as evidence.
Some geographic facts summarize earlier literature; the article is an original geosystem study, not an independent survey of every river name.
The stated length is not a measurement of the selected baseline fragments.

sources.agency_or_publisher: Al-Farabi Kazakh National University, KazNU Bulletin Geography series 2(37); research authors affiliated with L.N. Gumilyov Eurasian National University
sources.source_date_basis: Printed issue 2(37),2013, pp.76–85; fieldwork described as 2012–2013. PDF creation metadata is 2018 and is not publication date.
sources.read_location: Printed pp.76–78, Figure 1 on78, Figure 2 on80, and keyed field-site names on82.
sources.own_factual_extraction: This original field study supplies full-basin thematic maps and a named upper/middle/lower Sarysu framework. Its upper subdivisions include Zhaman-Sarysu and Zhaksy-Sarysu; the lower subdivision extends from the Kengir confluence to Lake Telikol. Figure 1 shows the east–west upper basin and the southward lower valley on a geographic grid. Figure 2 locates numbered field sites across the whole basin, with named keys elsewhere in the article, including Kairakty. Titles provide Russian, Kazakh and English river usage. Neither map labels every river segment or defines the exact transition between headwater names.

sources.own_factual_extraction: The government reports a specific flood-management flow of 200–250 m³/s from Kengir reservoir through the Sarysu in Ulytau toward Lake Telikol in Kyzylorda. This independently establishes contemporary official Russian river usage and a real operational connection to the terminal-lake region. It does not establish perennial flow or locate the baseline endpoint on a lake shoreline.
scope_limits: A dated operational statement, not a current discharge observation or formal naming decision.
No full-river map, headwater-name boundary or exact mouth coordinate is provided.
